# qa-classifications.md — UNICEF RFP RFPS-DAN-2021-503347 (notice 146988)
#
# Source: the consolidated "Q & A.pdf" clarifications document (27 entries).
# This file is SUPPLEMENTARY to the Q&A PDF — it adds per-entry classifications so the
# Sprint 1 manifest loader can distinguish binding clarifications from informational
# restatements when building the rubric.
#
# Fields:
#   classification: binding | informational | noise
#   touches:        scoring_rubric (<criterion>) | submission_requirement | commercial_term | (blank)
#   supersedes:     (optional) entry id this one overrides
#
#   binding        = changes/clarifies how a bid is prepared or SCORED
#   informational  = real context; no effect on bid preparation or scoring (incl. restated cost allocation)
#   noise          = off-topic / empty / pure restatement
# HIGHEST-VALUE labels: entries that clarify the NUMBERED technical evaluation rubric (1.2, 1.4)
# or submission requirements (7.1.4a, 7.1.5). The base RFP ("RFPS 503347.pdf" on notice 135638) holds
# the rubric these reference.

---

## 1 — Technical
classification: informational
touches: commercial_term
content: |
  Q: Who pays residence cost in the countries where O.G.S. maintenance is done?
  A: UNICEF reimburses travel per UNICEF rules — most direct/economic transport (economy only), DSA
     (ICSC rates), terminal expenses, and miscellaneous (visa, airport tax, etc.).
  [Restates standard cost allocation; does not change how a bid is scored → informational.]

## 2 — Technical
classification: informational
touches: commercial_term
content: |
  Q: Who supplies the required spare parts — supplier or UNICEF?
  A: The bidding organisation is responsible for supply and procurement of spare parts.

## 3 — Technical
classification: informational
touches: commercial_term
content: |
  Q: If a local agent supplies parts, who negotiates price — supplier or UNICEF?
  A: Procurement of spare parts is the supplier's responsibility.

## 4 — Commercial
classification: informational
touches: commercial_term
content: |
  Q: Will taxes be deducted from financial dues after maintenance works?
  A: UNICEF does not withhold taxes; suppliers are responsible for their own taxes.

## 5 — Commercial
classification: informational
touches: commercial_term
content: |
  Q: Should we open a special offshore/external bank account, or can payment go to a local account?
  A: Generally no special offshore account required for this LTA; local regulations handled case by
     case. Proof of bank required at UNICEF vendor registration. Quotes and payments in USD.

## 6 — Technical
classification: informational
touches: 
content: |
  Q: Will UNICEF facilitate VISA approval procedures for the maintenance team?
  A: Generally visas (and travel) are the supplier's responsibility; UNICEF may assist in special
     circumstances. [Compare with entry 25 on visa fees — entry 25 supersedes this.]

## 7 — Commercial
classification: informational
touches: commercial_term
content: |
  Q: Define payment terms and conditions.
  A: UNICEF standard payment terms are 30 days net. Per-project payment schedules in the TOR, may be
     milestone/deliverable-based.

## 8 — Technical
classification: informational
touches: 
content: |
  Q: Will UNICEF provide approvals for carriage of calibration and inspection devices?
  A: Country-dependent; conditions defined in the project-specific TOR. UNICEF may assist in special
     circumstances.

## 9 — Commercial/Technical
classification: informational
touches: 
content: |
  Q: Is the tender based in Malawi?
  A: It is a global tender. UNICEF wants vendors who can serve ideally multiple regions; single-region
     suppliers are not excluded.

## 10 — Technical
classification: informational
touches: 
content: |
  Q: Do you already have the oxygen-plant locations?
  A: No. Global-services LTA; project-specific locations provided with the TORs.

## 11 — Commercial
classification: informational
touches: commercial_term
content: |
  Q: Clarity on the financial aspect of the project.
  A: Each project has a separate budget; LTA holders invited to quote per project TOR. UNICEF aims to
     create LTAs with qualified vendors for repair and biomedical engineering/technical services.

## 12 — Technical
classification: informational
touches: 
content: |
  Q: Which countries will be included?
  A: As yet unknown. UNICEF operates in 130 countries; the LTA will be available globally.

## 13 — Technical
classification: binding
touches: submission_requirement
content: |
  Q: Under 7.1.4a (Plant Repair Services), an indicative project plan with "approximate number of days"
     is required. (i) Should timelines reflect past projects or include a COVID-19 buffer? (ii) Guidance
     on assumed training scope?
  A: (i) Provide your best estimate for this year, allowing for current global delays. (ii) Training
     should suit hospital technicians and biomedical engineers, including some with limited/no
     experience with the equipment.

## 14 — Technical
classification: binding
touches: submission_requirement
content: |
  Q: Under 7.1.5, client references or case studies are requested. For references, is a client letter
     required, or just context + contact info for separate outreach?
  A: If case studies are submitted, UNICEF requires contact information to facilitate separate outreach.

## 15 — Technical
classification: binding
touches: scoring_rubric (1.2)
content: |
  Q: Under 1.2 of the technical evaluation rubric — how are years of experience calculated? If an org
     has 10y in some but not all of the 7.1.4a services, how is that scored?
  A: Provide estimated years considering the entire set of services; UNICEF reviews each case and the
     content of the work and scores accordingly. The rubric is indicative.
  [Directly clarifies SCORING criterion 1.2 — references base-RFP rubric.]

## 16 — Technical
classification: binding
touches: scoring_rubric (1.4)
content: |
  Q: Under 1.4 of the technical evaluation rubric — how is country reach calculated? Counted by # of
     countries with experience, or by geographic reach willing to serve?
  A: Scoring is based on where the organisation is willing and able to provide services; countries with
     experience are considered in the 'Technical Experience' section.
  [Directly clarifies SCORING criterion 1.4 — references base-RFP rubric.]

## 17 — Technical
classification: informational
touches: 
content: |
  Q: Is this only maintenance, or supply of new plant?
  A: This is an RFPS for a services LTA. UNICEF aims to tender supply of new plants later.

## 18 — Commercial/Technical
classification: binding
touches: scoring_rubric (country reach)
content: |
  Q: Can we bid for a specific country — what if it is a war zone?
  A: UNICEF seeks suppliers able to deploy across multiple countries/regions; points awarded by number
     of countries/regions served (per TOR). UNICEF may assist with security/special support in conflict
     zones; specifics in project TOR.
  [Touches country-reach SCORING.]

## 19 — Commercial
classification: informational
touches: commercial_term
content: |
  Q: Will there be several LTAs? Multiple quoting bids per project/country?
  A: Number of LTA holders not yet known; multiple bids possible in some regions. UNICEF hopes for
     global coverage.

## 20 — Commercial
classification: informational
touches: commercial_term
content: |
  Q: Is the LTA with Global UNICEF? Will contracts be made with country offices after quotation?
  A: Varies case by case. LTA lets country offices place their own POs, but initially contracts placed
     by Supply Division.

## 21 — Technical
classification: informational
touches: 
content: |
  Q: Is the RFP purely reactive maintenance, or also preventive?
  A: Primary focus is reactive repair; countries could prepare a TOR for more regular preventative work.
     [Answer appears truncated in source — verify.]

## 22 — Technical
classification: binding
touches: scoring_rubric (brand coverage)
content: |
  Q: Must a proposal cover multiple/all brands, or can it be brand-specific?
  A: UNICEF seeks suppliers who can repair the full range of plant brands. Single-brand capability must
     be clearly indicated and experience scored accordingly.
  [Touches brand-coverage SCORING.]

## 23 — Commercial/Technical
classification: binding
touches: scoring_rubric (country reach)
content: |
  Q: We only work in Yemen — can we bid just for Yemen?
  A: UNICEF seeks multi-country/region suppliers; points by number of countries/regions served (per
     TOR). Single-country bids allowed but scored accordingly; indicate neighbouring-country capability.
  [Touches country-reach SCORING.]

## 24 — Commercial/Technical
classification: binding
touches: scoring_rubric (country reach)
content: |
  Q: Can we bid for more than one country (some are interdependent, esp. West Africa)?
  A: UNICEF seeks multi-country/region suppliers; points by number of countries/regions served (per TOR).
  [Touches country-reach SCORING.]

## 25 — Commercial/Technical
classification: binding
touches: commercial_term
supersedes: 6
content: |
  Q: On VISA — though the supplier is responsible, will UNICEF cover the fees/costs?
  A: Yes. UNICEF will cover visa fees on presentation of receipt.
  [Modifies the cost position in entry 6 — a binding commercial clarification. supersedes: 6.]

## 26 — Commercial
classification: informational
touches: submission_requirement
content: |
  Q: Is subcontracting allowed?
  A: Yes — consult the RFPS document for the requirements when subcontracting.
  [Real answer about what a bid may contain; points to subcontracting requirements → informational,
   not noise.]

## 27 — Commercial
classification: informational
touches: 
content: |
  Q: Estimated timeline for LTAs to be established, and time between relationship establishment and the
     ToL process?
  A: UNICEF aims to complete evaluation/clarifications during September and have LTAs in place by October,
     accessible immediately by countries.
